findings.where: screen 3 (T3), the push picture's '1811 N' labels and the line under it, explain paragraph 3, whatAmILookingAt and the K.check label
findings.what: Checked by hand, '72.4 ÷ 0.04 = 1811 N' is wrong: 72.4 ÷ 0.04 = 1810, and the 1811 comes from the unrounded 72.44 N m. Write 1810 N everywhere, and set N.F from the rounded 72.4. 1810 × 0.2 = 362 N m still holds.

findings.where: screen 1 (lead, T1 and the line under the picture)
findings.what: The first screen reads about 140 words: the lead has 20, T1 has 87 and the line under the picture has 33. The line under the picture repeats T1's 'the pinion turns five times ... 1450 rev/min in, 290 rev/min out'. Cut T1 to about 60 words by dropping what the lead already says, or show the line under the picture only after the teeth have been dragged.

findings.where: screen 3 (the line under the push picture)
findings.what: The line under the picture ('The same 1811 N push acts five times further out ... 362 N m') repeats T3's last three sentences, so the screen reads 118 words and everything after the diagram is repetition. Drop it, or replace it with the one point T3 leaves out: 'That push back is the load the motor feels.'

The explain carries six footnote markers for five sources, which is more than a few. [^4] appears twice, once on the bold closing summary. [^2] (a belt that does not slip moves at the rim speed) and [^4] (the power out is smaller than the power in) are not values he would look up on a job. Keep [^1] (gear ratio), [^3] (rad/s) and [^5] (misalignment) and drop the rest.

findings.where: screens 5, 7 and 9 (the line under the picture)
findings.what: At the opening settings, the line under the picture repeats numbers the text has just given: 550 W and 10.45 kW, 15 and 96.7 rev/min and 981 N m, the 5 : 1 belt. That takes the screens to about 101, 108 and 101 words. Show the line only after a move, or cut the matching sentence from the text.

findings.where: screen 1 picture (also screens 5, 7 and 9): the drag knobs and the mesh dot
findings.what: The two drag knobs and the mesh dot are all filled navy dots. So 'the dot' in T1 could mean any of the three, and nothing tells him the knobs can be dragged. Give the knobs a handle look, such as a hollow ring or grip ticks, and write 'the small dot where the teeth meet'.

findings.where: gear screens, the 'teeth / 6.1 m/s' label under the pinion
findings.what: 'teeth' on its own is a cryptic label, and it sits below the pinion, away from the mesh dot it describes. Write 'both gears' teeth here: 6.1 m/s', or add a short leader line to the dot.

findings.where: the key above the power bar (screens 1, 5, 7 and 9, light and dark at 360 px)
findings.what: The word 'speed' runs into the torque arrow, so the key reads 'speed↷ torque'. Move the torque swatch about 10 units to the right, as the build log already notes.
The output end is labelled only 'out'. At 95% the bar hardly narrows, so the power that passes through cannot be read off the picture. Label it '10.45 kW out', updating live with the slider.
The 'push back' force is drawn in teal, which the key gives to speed, so it can read as a speed. Draw both pushes in the force and torque navy, or in a third colour.

'Torque goes the other way' is vague for an opening. Lead with the point: 'The torque rises by the same ratio of 5.' In 'That push acts on the wheel's tooth, and it pushes back just as hard', 'it' could mean either tooth. Write 'The wheel's tooth pushes back just as hard.'
'At 95% each, about 90% gets through' skips the step. Write '0.95 × 0.95 = 0.90, so about 90% gets through.'
'open belt' is used without saying what one is. Write 'A plain loop of belt, called an open belt, turns both pulleys the same way.'

The lesson never says what a coupling is, although couplings are in its title. The screen titled 'Lining up shafts' also opens on a second idea, that the slow shaft is thicker. Lead with 'A coupling joins the ends of two shafts so one drives the other', then alignment. Move the thick-shaft point to the finish line.

The brief set 'misalignment does not cost measurable motor efficiency' as one of the lesson's checks, and the US DOE note is in the research. The lesson leaves it out. One sentence would fit once the thick-shaft sentences move: 'It barely changes the motor's efficiency. The harm is wear and heat.'

T5 says 'Its torque drops from 362 N m to 344 N m', but the readouts follow any dragged teeth: the moved shot at 33 and 66 teeth reads 138 N m beside that sentence. Write 'With 20 and 100 teeth, its torque drops from 362 N m to 344 N m.'
T1 opens with the setup, and the point arrives only in sentence five. Open with it: 'The bigger gear turns slower, by the ratio of the teeth.'
